Per Court :-
 . Heard both sides finally with their consent.

2. Appellants are aggrieved by judgment and award dated
 01.04.2015 passed in L.A.R.No.210 of 2012 awarding rate of Rs.10,000/- per
 Hector for the land acquired.

The predominant submission of the appellants is
 that the Reference Court held the appellants entitled to compensation at the
 rate of Rs.27,000/- per Hector but awarded only 10,000/- per Hector as the
 claim was restricted to avoid payment of court fees.

It is submitted that the
 approach of the learned Judge is arbitrary.

It is candidly stated by learned
 counsel that his clients are ready to pay deficit court fees.
Learned counsel Mr. Surwase for respondent no.2 would support

sentences.text:
It is submitted that no interference is called for and
appellants are estopped from claiming any enhancement.

4. I have gone through the Record and Proceeding and the
impugned judgment.

The memo of the reference indicates that the claim was
restricted to the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Hector.

The Reference Court in the
impugned judgment and award categorically observed that the appellants are
entitled Rs.27,000/- per Hector.

The only reason which is appearing from
paragraph 34 of the impugned judgment is the restriction of the claim by the
appellants in the Reference Court.

This type of approach is not in consonance
with the law laid down in Indore Development Authority vs. Tarak Singh and
Others reported in 1995 Supp (3) Supreme Court Cases 25 and
Chandrashekhar and Others vs. Additional Special Land Acquisition Officer
reported in (2009) 14 Supreme Court Cases 441.
5.

sentences.text:
Once the Reference Court has come to conclusion that the
appellants are entitled to Rs.27,000/- per Hector, they would have been called
upon to pay the deficit court fees.

It further reveals that the interest is
awarded from the date of notification instead of awarding it from 25.06.1984.
Therefore, it is desirable to allow the appeal with certain modifications.
 (3) 142 Fa 2261 Of 2023
 Order
 a.
First Appeal is allowed.

b. The appellants shall be entitled to rate of Rs.27,000/- per
 Hector for the land acquired.

c. The appellants shall not be entitled to the interest and
statutory benef
its for the delayed period

. d. The appellants shall be entitled to the interest under Section 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 as per full Bench Judgment in State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari [2016 AIR (Bom.)141].
e. Save and except above, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court shall stand unaltered.
